node.label: Mary Louise Pratt
node.date_label: “Arts of the Contact Zone” (1991) · Imperial Eyes: Travel Writing and Transculturation (1992) · Planetary Longings (2022)
node.description: Develops the contact zone as a way to examine encounters structured by unequal power. In the selected opening of “Arts of the Contact Zone,” colonial writing becomes a site of appropriation and response rather than an exchange between self-contained, homogeneous cultures. Her reading of Guaman Poma’s New Chronicle identifies autoethnography: subordinated subjects selectively use dominant genres and languages to address external representations and different audiences. This is Pratt’s particular reading of an Andean text; its historical details and contemporary Indigenous identities are not automatically certified by her theorization. The original article supplies the argument, while later book metadata supplies distinct publication facts.
